content.text:
This figure is from AC 43.13-2B, Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices: Aircraft Alterations. Its caption: "FIGURE 9-14. TYPICAL WING CARRY-THROUGH INSTALLATION".
Describe it for a mechanic who can't see it: say what it shows, then transcribe every label,
value, unit, part number, and note printed in it. Don't add anything that isn't in the figure.
If it shows nothing of use (a logo, a signature, a blank area), say so in one sentence.

message.content:
The figure shows three views of a typical wing carry-through installation: an upper-left detail of a clevis fitting with a bolt and nut, a lower-left view of a carry-through structure suspended beneath a wing spar with multiple bolts and a clevis at the bottom, and a right-side view of a wing spar section with a fitting attached and a bolted connection.

No labels, values, units, part numbers, or notes are printed in the figure.
